question: Should OpenClaw expose a public post-subagent-completion/pre-announcement hook, and if so should it be a narrow subagent hook or part of a generic output/delivery boundary?
rationale: The missing hook is source-proven, but exposing child results and allowing announcement mutation or suppression changes plugin API, message delivery, session-state, and sensitive-data boundaries that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design Generic Delivery Boundary
options.body: Define one minimized output/delivery interception seam that covers subagent completions and other guarded delivery needs before adding public hook names.

options.title: Add Narrow Subagent Hook
options.body: Add a typed post-subagent-completion/pre-announcement hook with tightly scoped event fields, explicit return semantics, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep Observation-Only Hooks
options.body: Keep subagent_ended observation-only and solve fallback notification, suppression, and filtering through separate delivery-policy issues.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Define one minimized output/delivery interception seam that covers subagent completions and other guarded delivery needs before adding public hook names.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook contract and security-sensitive plugin API history makes this the strongest available owner for the payload and authority decision.
